clue.text: Left wearing apprentice’s suit

indicators.note: a wearer has the garment round them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cub is a raw beginner or trainee, as in cub reporter; the apostrophe-s supplies the final letter
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A trainee is dressed in a formal two-piece outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The L sits inside CUBS, with the apostrophe-s read as the final S. 'Suit' is the card sense, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four card suits in a standard deck, alongside hearts, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Punctuation mark needs deleting initially, editor ordered

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words just before it

blocks.note: a common punctuation mark
the first letters of these two words
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A sub-editor demands that a stray comma be struck out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deleting' looks like an instruction to remove something, but it only contributes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have commanded someone is to have given them an instruction they must obey.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready for trouble

blocks.note: someone out of bed is up
as in ready, steady, go: all set

explanation.surface: Someone already up and dressed is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to upset someone is to trouble or distress them.

clue.text: Horse crossing motorway twice halted

indicators.note: the horse spans the other letters, holding them within itself

blocks.note: a steed is a horse, especially a spirited one
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1; twice gives two of them

explanation.surface: A horse that tries to cross a motorway twice gets stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' looks like the horse walking over the road, but it means straddling letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or stop it, so stemmed means halted.

clue.text: Hooked by peculiar instrument

blocks.note: caught, as an animal in a trap
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone is captivated by an odd musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the old British adjective meaning odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its lower head.

clue.text: Insults missing Liberal’s spectacles

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: slights are snubs or insults
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician's glasses are mocked by rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are things worth seeing, and the sights of a city are its notable attractions.

clue.text: Stopped a run and relaxed

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
rested means took it easy

explanation.surface: A jogger halted the run to take a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arrested has been halted or checked, as in arrested development.

clue.text: Radical old male hiding in tree

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is concealed inside it

blocks.note: ex- means former
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A former man is concealed up a tree, behaving like a militant.
explanation.walkthrough: Old gives the prefix meaning former, as in an ex-husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical views and extreme views both lie far from the moderate mainstream.

clue.text: Gives an account of embracing four nieces?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to relate a story is to tell it
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone tells a story about four nieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags nieces as only one example of the wider group defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Nieces are family members, an example of the broader class of kin.

clue.text: Beeb only half supporting prime minister, perhaps

indicators.note: keeping only half means the rest of the word is dropped
in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath the one above it

blocks.note: Theresa May was UK prime minister from 2016 to 2019
the Beeb is a nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The BBC is only half-heartedly backing the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of Beeb goes below MAY in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are interchangeable adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty.

clue.text: Emissary from German city in car with gears oddly missing

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it
with the odd-numbered letters missing, only the even ones remain

blocks.note: MG is a British make of car
Essen is a city in the Ruhr
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An envoy arrives from Germany in a car whose gearbox is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: MG is a classic British sports-car marque; the German city goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is someone sent with a message or mission on another's behalf, a courier.

clue.text: Count it all yourself? Not all

indicators.note: not all of the phrase is used, only a stretch running across its words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of it, all of all and the start of yourself

explanation.surface: A challenge to do all the counting alone, but not all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a tally means recording a running score of items, as on a scorecard or notched stick.

clue.text: Try a lure behind tail of trout

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
one piece placed behind another comes after it

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter
to lure is to entice or tempt

explanation.surface: An angler tries putting a lure just behind a trout's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort or go at something, just as a try is.

clue.text: Piece of confectionery, darling?

blocks.note: first meaning: a British word for a small sugary treat, a candy
second meaning: a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sweet is candy, and a sweetie is the childish form of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a candy and, affectionately, a dear person one is fond of.

clue.text: Group of detectives in river come to a conclusion

indicators.note: one group placed in the other is enclosed by it

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another runs through Chester
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police detectives in a river reach a verdict on a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to settle on a judgement or choice after thinking it over.

clue.text: These could be used for recording lawsuits about badger’s home

definitions.text: These could be used for recording

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: legal cases brought before a court
a sett is the burrow a badger lives in

explanation.surface: Tapes are used to record lawsuits concerning a badger's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassettes are tape cartridges once widely used to store audio from radio or microphone.

clue.text: Reticent about first tennis shot by daughter

indicators.note: placed by means set next to, so the last piece follows

blocks.note: re means concerning
every tennis point begins with a serve
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shy girl is uneasy about her opening shot at tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is quiet and holds back their feelings, like someone reticent.

clue.text: Cleaner animal accepting lead from the bloke

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so it goes inside
the lead of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a common animal
the first letter
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A cleaner animal is taking a dog lead from the man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is the noun, a cleaning agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, the soap-like substance used for washing clothes and dishes.

clue.text: Most tipsy maiden retires drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A very tipsy young woman goes off to bed, drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild British euphemism for slightly drunk, so merriest is the tipsiest.

clue.text: Abandoned novel deters Edward

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take on a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A neglected book puts off a reader called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserted has been left behind and forsaken, exactly as something abandoned has.

clue.text: Swap Queen record with large crack

blocks.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
an EP is an extended-play record
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a crack shot is an ace, an expert

explanation.surface: Someone exchanges a Queen album for a badly cracked one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' means first-rate here, as in a crack shot, not a split.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to swap it for another item of the same kind.

clue.text: Secret place to put your clothes

blocks.note: first meaning: hidden or undeclared
second meaning: a cupboard or wardrobe

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a hidden wardrobe, but the first word is a separate adjective meaning concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both concealed or private, as an adjective, and a small storage cupboard or wardrobe.

clue.text: Learner driver frets, avoiding wide vehicles

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
to fret is to worry
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A nervous learner driver steers well clear of wide trucks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide' looks like it describes the vehicles, but it is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries are the British name for trucks, large goods vehicles on the road.

clue.text: Do ripe bananas stretch?

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether ripe bananas get longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A period is a span of time, as is a stretch, such as a stretch in prison.

clue.text: Look around rear of hotel for a kipper

indicators.note: one piece around another holds it within
the rear of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: to look is to see
the last letter
per means for each, as in a pound per person

explanation.surface: Someone peers round the back of a hotel in search of a smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like the smoked herring, but it is someone who kips, British slang for sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To kip is British slang for to sleep, so a kipper is one who sleeps.

clue.text: Salesman’s turned up holding a weapon

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
to hold something is to keep it inside

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative; the apostrophe-s adds the plural S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A salesman arrives carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long weapon with a pointed head, thrown or thrust by hand.

clue.text: Peer and I were bare, previously

indicators.note: stripped bare, a word loses its outer letters and keeps its core

blocks.note: an earl is a British nobleman, a peer
taken as written
the middle letters

explanation.surface: A nobleman confesses that the two of them were naked in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning look, but it is a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and previously both mean at a prior time, before now.

clue.text: Photograph part of leg a minx raised

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase is used, a run of consecutive letters
in a down entry, raised means read upwards, in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of leg through a into minx

explanation.surface: A flirtatious woman lifts her leg for a camera shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph is a picture, and an image is any visual picture or representation.

clue.text: Particularly cross after eastern craft returned

indicators.note: placed after means coming next in the sequence
something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
X is a cross shape
craft and art both mean skill

explanation.surface: Someone is especially angry after an Eastern boat came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry and 'craft' like a boat; they are X and skill.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, extra means especially, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Get rid of evil alien I met

indicators.note: evil means bad or corrupt, so the letters are twisted out of shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to destroy a wicked extraterrestrial the speaker encountered.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove or dispose of it entirely.

clue.text: Thought highly of new diet with crepes? Not I!

indicators.note: not I says a letter is excluded from the set
new means made afresh, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders about a new regime involving pancakes, then declines.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I from diet with crepes, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To be respected is to be held in high esteem or admired by others.

clue.text: Fish disappear after start of season

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
placed after means following in the sequence

blocks.note: the first letter
to melt away is to vanish

explanation.surface: Fish vanish once the season opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small silvery food fish found in northern waters.
